headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading error: unstructured can read/write files and egress to allowlisted services, while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and cannot verify or contain its outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: python-cheatsheet has no input surfaces, so it cannot be directly injected. unstructured can read documents and process file content, so if its outputs are manually copied into the cheatsheet workflow, prompt-like content could be misread. The pathway is weak and requires unusual bridging, not a default shared channel.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies unstructured output into a downstream prompt or note-taking workflow
IF unstructured processes attacker-controlled document text that is later treated as instructions
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Treat document text as untrusted data
Use a fixed prompt template that strips instructions from pasted content

B_data_leakage.rationale: unstructured reads filesystem documents and can send API calls over allowlisted egress, so sensitive file contents could leave the local environment. python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and does not itself leak data, but pairing it with unstructured creates a workflow where extracted content may be exposed through the latter's network path. The interaction is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are processed by unstructured
IF unstructured sends extracted content to any allowlisted external service
mitigations: Disable network egress for the processing job
Separate sensitive and non-sensitive document pipelines

C_capability_conflict.rationale: python-cheatsheet cannot write or modify state, but unstructured can read and write files and supports multiple instances. If both are pointed at the same directory, unstructured can overwrite or race on shared artifacts while the cheatsheet remains passive. The conflict is real for the pair because only one agent has mutable access, but shared workspace use makes it operationally risky.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to use the same writable directory
IF multiple unstructured instances run concurrently on shared files
mitigations: Run only one unstructured instance per workspace
Use read-only mounts for the cheatsheet environment

D_cascading_error.rationale: unstructured produces parsed document outputs that downstream consumers may treat as authoritative. python-cheatsheet is not an evaluator and cannot verify those outputs, so if its content is used as reference material in a workflow, errors can propagate into later actions. The pair lacks a built-in verification step, making cascading mistakes plausible.
conditions: IF unstructured output is used as input to a downstream decision or publication step
IF no human or automated verification checks the extracted text
mitigations: Add a validation step before publication
Require human review of extracted fields
Compare extracted text against source documents
Flag low-confidence parses for manual inspection

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent. python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and touches no data classes, while unstructured processes documents and exposes privacy-policy/docs endpoints. Because the pairwise compliance pathway is not evidenced, only a low residual risk remains from generic document-processing governance gaps.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed through unstructured
IF the operator requires a residency or retention guarantee not documented here
mitigations: Avoid regulated data until a DPA is in place
